reply_text:
Reviewed `receipt-lines` (`a6c40d4`) against `main`. Two findings:

1. **P1 — Printed prices are 100× too high** — `receipt/render.py:2`
   `format_money` formats integer cents directly as dollars: `format_money(1299)` returns `$1299.00`, not `$12.99`. Every rendered item inherits this. Convert cents to dollars before formatting, and add a literal expected-value assertion—the current test compares against the same broken formatter, so it passes.

2. **P2 — Rendered item amounts aren’t right-aligned** — `receipt/render.py:7`
   `render_line` pads the name to 20 characters instead of using the new 32-column `align` helper. Amounts of different lengths end in different columns, and item rows don’t align with totals produced by `align`. Route item rendering through the shared layout logic and test that different-sized amounts end at column 32.

All **3 existing tests pass**, but they miss these defects. I’d fix the money formatting before merging. No files changed.
